findings.message: `/devcontainer up` and `/devcontainer build` never carry the selected `--config`, so AC-2 is only half met. `handlers["up"]` (src/commands.ts) calls `services.execution.up({ operation: "up", initiator: "slash-command", workspace })` and `handlers["build"]` does the same, while `configPath` reaches the adapter only (a) for `exec`, via the frozen bound selection, or (b) when a caller hand-builds an `UpBuildRequest` with it — which no command-layer caller does. Consequence: in a workspace whose only configuration is a named `.devcontainer/<name>/devcontainer.json` or the legacy root `devcontainer.json`, `/devcontainer up` sends the CLI nothing it can resolve and the start fails, which is the very defect this change set out to fix. My own unit test (container-config-routing.test.ts, "passes an explicit configPath through up and build") drives the SERVICE with a literal request, so it pinned the seam rather than the wiring. Fix: resolve the configuration for the requested workspace in the `up`/`build` handlers (registry entry → selected candidate, or the entry's default candidate) and pass `configPath`, then assert it by invoking the command handler.

`selectionFor(entry, candidateId, configPath?)` accepts its third argument unvalidated: `const resolvedConfig = configPath ?? (needsExplicitConfig(entry.configKind) && entry.configPath.length > 0 ? entry.configPath : undefined)`. Validation against the discovered set lives only in `resolveConfigCandidate`, at its current call site. Today's single caller validates, so there is no live bypass — but the boundary itself permits an arbitrary path to become `--config <path>` in the CLI argv, which makes the CLI read an arbitrary file as DevContainer configuration. Validate inside `selectionFor` (reject anything not present in `entry.configCandidates`) or remove the parameter and pass a resolved candidate.

`dormantHostBash` (extensions/index.ts) reimplements the host shell with `spawn(command, { shell: true, cwd, env: process.env })`. Reachable only after `/devcontainer off` disengages a session whose routed `bash` tool is already registered. It does not widen access relative to a Pi without this extension (both end up running a host shell — and at session start, when dormant, no replacement is registered at all), but it does mean the LLM-facing `bash` tool then has THIS extension's shell choice (`sh -c`), output bound, and a full inherited environment including any provider keys present in the Pi process, rather than Pi's built-in semantics. Recommend not reimplementing: delegate to the built-in definition, or at minimum pass the same minimal env the rest of the extension builds (PATH/HOME/XDG) instead of `process.env`, and document the delta.

`missingAcceptanceMatrix: true` persists: `.kata/tasks/activation-and-config-mechanism/task.json` still carries the placeholder `AC-1: "Implement the change successfully."`, while the real ten-criterion matrix (AC-1..AC-10) exists only in `openspec/changes/activation-and-config-mechanism/design.md`. The verification result therefore reported `acceptanceResults: [{ id: "AC-1", result: "PASS" }]`, which is a check of the placeholder, not of the change. Before judging, either sync the matrix into `task.json` (a task-store mutation) or record an explicit decision that the design document is the authoritative matrix.

Three behaviors shipped in this change are implemented but not isolated by any test in this environment: (1) dormancy at session start (nothing registered in a workspace without DevContainer evidence), (2) `engageDevcontainerSurfaces` registering tools from a command handler and Pi honoring that on the next turn, (3) the latency/impact of the bounded Docker probe for activation chain step 4. The capability-gated suites do exercise the real packed extension in a real Pi session (`loads the extension and registers the devcontainer tool surface`) and the full real-Docker run is green (10/10), which supports the wiring but does not isolate these three. They are documented as unverified in the design notes rather than claimed as verified.

`workspaceDrift` reports `openspec/changes/activation-and-config-mechanism/design.md` as outside the sealed revision scope: the artifact that authorizes the change is not co-versioned with the code it authorizes. Either add the design path to the owned paths at seal time or accept the drift explicitly, so a later reader can tell which design text corresponds to this revision.
